record.original_question: If the quadratic polynomial P_c is nonrecurrent, does there exist a conformal metric of the form rho(z)|dz| with integrable singularities for which P_c is expanding on its Julia set?

evidence.quote: Question 13. If Pc is nonrecurrent does this imply the existence of a conformal metric (a metric of the form ρ(z)|dz| with integrable singularities) for which Pc is expanding on its Julia set? [Yoccoz has proved local connectivity in the nonrecurrent case.]

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P_c(z) = z^2 + c$ be a quadratic polynomial on the complex plane, and let $J(P_c)$ denote its Julia set. Assume that $P_c$ is nonrecurrent, meaning that the critical point $0$ is not in the $\omega$-limit set of its own forward orbit under $P_c$.

A conformal metric on a neighborhood $U$ of $J(P_c)$ is an expression of the form $\rho(z)\,|dz|$, where $\rho$ is a non-negative measurable function whose singularities are integrable (i.e. $\rho$ may vanish or blow up, but $\int_K \rho^2\,dA < \infty$ on compact sets, and more generally the singularities give finite length to short curves). The map $P_c$ is said to be expanding with respect to $\rho(z)\,|dz|$ on $J(P_c)$ if there exist constants $\lambda > 1$ and $n_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $z$ in $J(P_c)$,
$$\rho(P_c^{n_0}(z))\,|(P_c^{n_0})'(z)| \;\ge\; \lambda\,\rho(z).$$

Question: Does the nonrecurrence of $P_c$ imply the existence of such a conformal metric $\rho(z)\,|dz|$ with integrable singularities for which $P_c$ is expanding on $J(P_c)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is answered affirmatively by the work of Carleson, Jones and Yoccoz ("Julia and John", 1994) and subsequent results in the theory of semi-hyperbolic rational maps. A quadratic polynomial is nonrecurrent (with no parabolic cycle) precisely when it is semi-hyperbolic, and semi-hyperbolic rational maps are known to be expanding with respect to a conformal metric with integrable singularities (an orbifold-type metric) on a neighborhood of the Julia set. This is standard in the theory of conformal fractals (Przytycki–Urbański).

status_evidence.title: Julia and John (Carleson, Jones, Yoccoz)
status_evidence.snippet: A recent result of L. Carleson, P.W. Jones and J.C. Yoccoz shows that the basin of attraction of a polynomial f is a John domain if and only if f is semihyperbolic.
status_evidence.claim: Carleson–Jones–Yoccoz characterize semi-hyperbolic polynomials, the class that for quadratics coincides with the nonrecurrent (no parabolic) case, and provide expanding metric estimates.

status_evidence.title: Conformal Fractals: Ergodic Theory Methods (Przytycki–Urbański)
status_evidence.snippet: Expansion can be characterized by ∥f′∥ > 1 with respect to a smooth conformal metric ρ defined near X, such as the metric ρ = σ + f*σ + ··· (f^(n-1))*σ.
status_evidence.claim: Semi-hyperbolic / nonrecurrent rational maps admit an expanding conformal metric with integrable singularities near their Julia sets.
